To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the gravitational field of the plane is a Rindler gravitational field, 2) the Rindler gravitational fields are the only static plane gravitational fields that are vacuum and 3) the Rindeler gravitational fields are the counterparts of the Newtonian uniform gravitational fields.

(i) the sources of static vacuum solutions with reflection symmetry are described by the Riemann tensor of the Rindler spacetime, (ii) the sources of the Schwarzschild vacuum solution are the gravitational field and the test particles of the Rindlerspace-time and (iii) the sources of all other static vacuum solutions with plane symmetry are the gravitational field of the Rindlervacuum and the test particles in it.
the gravitational field of the Newtonian plane is described by the Riemannian metric of the Rindler space-time, and the test particle moving in this field has constant acceleration.

, the Rindler space-time is the most appropriate solution for the gravitational field of massive plane, and the Newtonian theory is the limit of the Einstein theory when the mass is very small.

, contrary to the Newtonian theory of gravity, in general relativity, the sources of a uniform gravitational field are not Newtonian plane symmetric bodies, but rather Rindler plane symmetric bodies.

the Rindler metric is the only solution to the Einstein field equations that can be interpreted in terms of a uniform gravitational field in a plane.
